priorStories.headline: U.S. strikes Iranian positions on Qeshm Island
priorStories.body:
The U.S. carried out limited strikes against Iranian targets on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to American officials. One official said the targets included surface-to-air missile positions that threatened U.S. assets.

Iranian state media reported explosions on the island. U.S. Central Command had not publicly announced the operation when the reports were published.

priorStories.headline: Court declines to segregate California ballots
priorStories.body:
The Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s emergency request to separate about 20,000 California mail ballots from voters it alleged might not be citizens. The justices gave no explanation for their decision, which came one day before the November 3 midterm election.

California officials said the federal list contained extensive errors and that last-minute segregation could prevent eligible voters’ ballots from being counted.

priorStories.headline: Russian strikes kill 26 at Kherson aid sites
priorStories.body:
Ukrainian authorities said Russian bombing of an aid distribution center and a neighboring shelter in the southern Kherson region killed 26 people.

The attacks followed the expiration of a limited ceasefire that had allowed aid deliveries and evacuations in front-line and Russian-occupied areas.

priorStories.headline: New York reports child’s measles-linked death
priorStories.body:
New York health officials said a child had died in association with the state’s ongoing measles outbreak, the first known measles-associated death there in more than 30 years.

The state had recorded 178 cases through October 24. Officials urged residents to confirm that they were current on measles, mumps and rubella vaccinations.

sources.name: New York State Department of Health

candidates.summary: Ukrainian authorities said the death toll from Monday’s Russian strike on a humanitarian aid facility and shelter in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, rose to 31 on Tuesday. More than 45 residents remained missing as rescuers searched the site. Officials said the dead included four police officers and two rescue workers.
candidates.title: Ukraine raises Zaporizhzhia aid-site strike toll to 31

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump said the United States would stop providing about $4 billion in annual aid to Israel in 2027 while continuing to sell the country military hardware. Trump said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had approached him about the change; Netanyahu’s office did not immediately comment.
candidates.title: Trump says U.S. will end annual aid to Israel in 2027

candidates.summary: The Justice Department said it deployed approximately 1,000 election monitors and observers across all 50 states, describing it as the largest monitoring effort in department history and its first covering every state. The Civil Rights Division coordinated the operation to monitor compliance with federal voting-rights laws.
candidates.title: Justice Department deploys election monitors in all 50 states

candidates.summary: Greenland’s parliament voted 16-0, with seven abstentions, to approve a security agreement with Denmark and the United States that could allow more U.S. bases while keeping Greenland under Danish control. The agreement will not enter into force until the remaining parliamentary processes in the Kingdom of Denmark are completed.
candidates.title: Greenland parliament approves U.S.-Denmark security agreement

sources.name: Associated Press via The Washington Post

candidates.summary: Spanish Transport Minister Óscar Puente announced his resignation during a parliamentary appearance about an October 28 high-speed train collision south of Madrid that killed 69 people. Puente said he decided to resign immediately after the crash. Earlier Tuesday, he announced measures intended to improve rail safety.
candidates.title: Spanish transport minister resigns after fatal rail crash

sources.name: Associated Press via The Washington Post

candidates.summary: Indonesian police said they detained three senior police generals suspected of illegally intercepting communications belonging to President Prabowo Subianto and other public figures. Police said the investigation concerns unauthorized access, interception and deletion of electronic data. The three officers had not publicly responded to the allegations.
candidates.title: Indonesia detains three police generals in wiretapping investigation

sources.name: Associated Press via The Washington Post

candidates.summary: Former U.S. government contractor Abraham Teklu Lemma pleaded guilty to conspiring to transmit national-defense information to Ethiopia. The Justice Department said Lemma removed classified information from government systems and facilities. Under the plea agreement, he agreed to a prison term of between 120 and 262 months; sentencing is scheduled for April 14, 2027.
candidates.title: Former U.S. contractor pleads guilty to spying for Ethiopia

candidates.summary: Federal prosecutors charged Oklahoma City resident Robin Patrick Martin with conveying false or misleading information and mailing threatening communications. Authorities alleged that he was connected to hundreds of letters, many containing nonhazardous white powder, sent to election officials, members of Congress, media organizations and others. The complaint remains an allegation.
candidates.title: Oklahoma man charged over threatening powder letters

candidates.summary: Lockheed Martin agreed to pay approximately $29.5 million through settlements announced by the Justice Department and Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. The agreements resolve allegations involving employment discrimination and false certifications of compliance with federal civil-rights requirements while Lockheed served as a federal contractor. The government said the allegations produced no determination of liability.
candidates.title: Lockheed Martin agrees to $29.5 million discrimination settlements

candidates.summary: CBS News projected that Democrats won control of the U.S. Senate after securing enough Republican-held seats to overturn the GOP’s 53-47 majority. Projected Democratic pickups included Texas, North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa, while the party retained seats in Georgia and New Hampshire. The final size of the Democratic majority remained undetermined.
candidates.title: Democrats win control of U.S. Senate

candidates.summary: Georgia voters elected Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, making her the first Black woman elected governor of a U.S. state and Georgia’s first governor of color. New Mexico elected Democrat Deb Haaland, a citizen of the Laguna Pueblo, as the first Native American woman to serve as a U.S. governor.
candidates.title: Georgia and New Mexico elect governors in historic firsts

candidates.summary: Democrats won control of the North Carolina House, ending the Republican majority in that chamber, and flipped the Wisconsin Senate. The North Carolina result gives Democratic Gov. Josh Stein a legislative majority in one chamber, while the Wisconsin result ended unified Republican control of the state Legislature.
candidates.title: Democrats flip legislative chambers in North Carolina and Wisconsin

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump congratulated Democrats for their election victories and said he would accept the results. In phone interviews, Trump said Democrats had campaigned well but maintained that Republican losses were not a referendum on him and blamed losing candidates rather than his administration’s policies.
candidates.title: Trump says he will accept midterm election results

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump said the United States would stop providing about $4 billion in annual aid to Israel in 2027 while continuing arms sales. Trump said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had approached him about the change. The current aid agreement runs through 2028, and the Associated Press reported that an abrupt cutoff would require congressional involvement and may not be feasible on Trump’s stated timetable.
candidates.title: Trump says U.S. will end annual aid to Israel in 2027
